subject: business-studies
title: Market Research Stretch Adventure
welcome_lead: Exam-style stretch. Evaluate the usefulness of research, big-data trends and ethics of data.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies stretch — evaluating research usefulness, big-data trends and data ethics.
final_note: You can evaluate the usefulness, accuracy and ethics of market research data.

concepts.def: Very large datasets analysed for patterns
Whether the same result would happen again
Whether the data measures what was intended
Law protecting how personal data is used
Middle value when data is ordered

walkthroughs.body_html:
Useful research is accurate, recent, relevant, and unbiased.

Always question: who collected it, when, how big a sample, what was the question?

Big data from loyalty cards and websites tracks real behaviour, not what people say.

Firms personalise offers, predict demand and spot trends — but must obey GDPR.

Mean can be skewed by outliers. Median is more representative when data is uneven.

Always tell the examiner WHY you chose the measure you did.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary market research?
options: Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
Primary research is the most important and secondary research is less important.
Primary research is original data the business gathers itself (surveys, interviews); secondary research uses existing data (reports, government statistics, market intelligence).
Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.

mcqs.q: What four growth strategies does Ansoff's Matrix identify?
options: Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.

Market penetration (existing product, existing market), market development (existing product, new market), product development (new product, existing market), diversification (new product, new market).
Ansoff's Matrix is about analysing competitors.
Ansoff's Matrix shows market share against profit.
